item: Row 421: "not analysed yet" is one shared count beside "not screened", and the figures built from the analysis say it
summary: R832 asked every aggregate surface to say how many imported articles the re-index has not finished, as the second reason beside not screened, never naming one article twice. The per-tab line, the Home strip and the Library breakdown already said it (#2394), but from the re-index backlog, which also counts articles queued for screening or quarantined. quarantine_scope.not_analysed_count is now the one notion: an article of an import still listed as merged with either analysis stamp of the current engine missing (the backlog's own test), minus the quarantined and the queued ones (screening wins), read at query time and reused 30 s per store; not_counted_tally carries it as not_analysed, so the stats, the Insights status line and the bulletin's backlog line state the disjoint count. Per figure, count_not_analysed counts the results a figure DOES count: the Explore keywords, When/Where/Who, sentiment, sources (their tone is the re-index's sentiment) and the mind map, and the conjunction panel, carry not_analysed_yet and draw "{n} of these results not analysed yet" (new key x12) with the existing hover. The dossier reaches articles only through their mentions, so it carries the corpus-wide count once. Commodity correlation, framing, Explore links and per-source article counts read no re-index output and say nothing. Measured on 1M imported articles, half stamped: 0.40 s for the whole-store count (the backlog read is 0.30 s), 16 ms for 1,001 result ids. No write, no schema change, no version bump.
